text:
alex: quick idea - 'micro-reinsert' path: small fastpath requests skip coalesce but can be reinserted into the next batch under a budget. goal: reuse KV warms without hurting long-request latency.

mira: seems plausible. main risk = next-batch bloat and H-O-L for long seq requests. how do you propose budget works?

sam: per-tenant token budget that accrues over time. each reinsert has a cost estimate. accept reinsert if budget >= cost. cheap checks, fair across tenants.

tj: add a local batch headroom guard too. if batch remaining headroom_ms < headroom_threshold, reject reinserts. two-layer guard: budget + headroom.

chen: also suggest affinity hints: fastpath attaches `kv_hint`. prefer joining batches whose affinity matches to avoid cross-warm churn. optional flag for rollout.

caroline: ran a micro-sim overnight with crude traffic. reinserts cut cold-KV miss rate ~26% for sub-50ms hits but p99 saw +5-8ms under peak. that matches H-O-L hypothesis.

alex: ok so conservative defaults: reinsert_enabled=false, when on use budget_rate=5tokens/s, headroom_threshold_ms=8ms, affinity_enabled=true, max_reinsert_items_per_tenant=30.

mira: operational metrics we need: reinsert_attempts, accept_rate, budget_balance_per_tenant, added_tokens_per_batch, p99_delta.post_reinsert. alert if p99_delta > 5% sustained 5m.

sam: cancellation semantics: remove from microqueue on client cancel and refund budget unless already executed. leaving gaps breaks packing.

tj: impl notes: microqueue flush only at batch cut points. that avoids mid-batch interference. merging at boundaries simplifies KV cache reuse ordering.

chen: also add a burst protection cap: per-tenant daily reinsertion quota or a leaky-bucket to prevent noisy tenants gaming credits.

infra-bot: perf-canary `micro-reinsert-canary` deployed by @caroline (3xA100). logs: https://internal.redwood/infra/micro-reinsert-canary

caroline: ran a controlled run - under uniform traffic reinserts reduce token cost by ~12% overall, but under skewed hotspots p99 delta grew by ~6ms. overall win depends heavily on traffic skew.

alex: decision: prototype conservative config (budget+headroom+affinity) and gather canary telemetry. if tail regresses, fall back to disabling reinserts.

tj: i'll spike the POC: batcher hook + budget check + headroom guard in 7 days. will include unit sim.

mira: i'll wire dashboards and an event stream for reinsertion rejections (reason=budget/headroom/affinity).

chen: i'll add a sim for affinity collision probability and measure cross-affinity pollution.

sam: ops: document rollback plan and a runtime flag to turn reinserts off quickly. also add canary runbook.

alex: perfect. tag as follow-up to continuous-batching refactor RFC. keep reinserts gated behind off-by-default flag and require clear canary pass before any rollout. :thumbsup:
